From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely.  There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda.  The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others.  It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be.  The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be.  The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice.  The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there.  You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.  On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily.  The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far.  For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well.  We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder.  I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual.  I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut.  It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud.  Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation.  Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet.  That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.  Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

Sentence (English): I installed the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater Nature Beige DUE5BGL2E built-in dishwasher through a home visit, and to cut to the chase, I'm incredibly satisfied.
Comments (English): I installed the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater Nature Beige DUE5BGL2E built-in dishwasher through a home visit, and to cut to the chase, I'm incredibly satisfied. My life has changed so much that I wonder how I ever lived without a dishwasher. At first, I was considering a 12-seater, but the answer is to just go with a 14-seater 3-tier one. You don't just put in plates and bowls; you also always end up with odds and ends like spoons, chopsticks, ladles, and scissors. With 3 tiers, the top spoon tray keeps everything organized, and the bottom compartment saves so much space that you can put a lot in at once. Ultimately, the bigger the capacity, the more convenient it is. Especially when guests come over or you're a few days behind, the 12-seater is likely to fill up quickly, which can be stressful. And there are various drying options, but I didn't necessarily go for the more expensive model with hot air drying. Considering the price difference, it was a bit of a waste of money. Instead, this model has TrueSteam, so it feels like it really focused on cleaning quality. Greasy dishes and stained pot lids come off much more cleanly, and I don't have to worry about odors. In my opinion, thorough cleaning is much more satisfying than excessive drying. The nature beige color really makes the kitchen look pretty, just like an objet d'art. The tones are refined without being flashy, and with the built-in design, the kitchen feels upgraded. The door installation was also done neatly, which put my mind at ease. Most of all, dishwashing time just disappears. Every time I saw the dishes pile up after eating, I was annoyed, but now I can just rinse them with water, put them in, press a button, and it's done, so stress-free. I use less water, my hands are less rough, and I save time, so the efficiency is amazing. If there's anyone considering a 12-person dishwasher, I'd like to tell them to just go with a 14-person, 3-tier dishwasher from the start. Comments (English): [ Beware of the Auto Door Open Feature ] || ---------------- || This one replaces a previous three rack KitchenAid dishwasher that we installed 10 to 12 years ago. First observations are that the door is lighter-weight, to the point of being tinny and unpleasant. The wire gauge used for the three wire racks is thinner and lighter weight as well, which causes the racks to twist and shake as you pull them in and out, again feeling cheap. On the positive side it cleans as advertised and the water spray feature on the third rack does a good job. The third rack is larger which means for us that the machine holds more… another good thing. First use on day one we had an issue with the automatic door opener (a plastic post not retracting) causing the door to not close but we weren't aware of this until we tried to close it fully for use a second time. Struggling to close the door for second use has now caused the door to sit slightly cockeyed, which is noticeable when open. We weren't aware able with online instructions to get the door opener deactivated but the door is still cockeyed. The machine is less than a month old. Works well, feels cheap and now looks cockeyed. Don't buy this model.

Sentence (English): So unsurprisingly our Samsung died almost on que, ten years after buying, much like the Washing machine that was a few months older, the Samsung Dishwasher had been having issues for a while with the door mechanism, then finally flashed the dreaded code for failed water heater.
Comments (English): [ Excellent Features, but a tad too noisy ] || ---------------- || So unsurprisingly our Samsung died almost on que, ten years after buying, much like the Washing machine that was a few months older, the Samsung Dishwasher had been having issues for a while with the door mechanism, then finally flashed the dreaded code for failed water heater. Given the time of year and limited funds these days, the nice fancy Bosch wasn't an option, and considering we not long ago got a Haier Washer that is perfectly ok, we figured either we get another Samsung, or we try out this brand and see how we go. It did take nearly two weeks to come, which I was quite disappointed about, looking at your Farmers.co.nz, you should carry stock. but I digress.From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely. There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda. The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others. It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be. The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be. The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice. The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there. You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

It did take nearly two weeks to come, which I was quite disappointed about, looking at your Farmers.co.nz, you should carry stock... but I digress.From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely. There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda. The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others. It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be. The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be. The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice. The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there. You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

It did take nearly two weeks to come, which I was quite disappointed about, looking at your Farmers.co.nz, you should carry stock. but I digress.From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely. There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda. The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others. It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be. The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be. The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice. The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there. You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

It did take nearly two weeks to come, which I was quite disappointed about, looking at your Farmers.co.nz, you should carry stock... but I digress.From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely. There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda. The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others. It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be. The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be. The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice. The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there. You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

It did take nearly two weeks to come, which I was quite disappointed about, looking at your Farmers.co.nz, you should carry stock. but I digress.From the outset you can see this dishwasher is cheaper, the sliding drawers are a bit clunky and are far from smooth, the height adjust for the top shelf is really weird and is not even close to the quality of the same thing on a samsung or better, rather you sort of have to pull it right out then wedge it back onto the runners on different wheels, very odd, a drawer with some brackets on the side would be so much easier Haier and it can't cost so much more surely. There is no water leak guard device built into the inlet hose so you're connect direct from the tap to the machine which lets hope isn't a problem is this town with very high water pressure.The overall design however if fine, its a nice colour, Satina, which is basically a plastic version of grey stainless steel, kinda. The buttons are all touch, and the controls are simple and make sense, you cycle through by way of a small orange LED above each option, Auto, Heavy, Medium, Glass etc etc, and below those you have the 'modifier' options which include extra dry (Awesome), Sanitise and a couple of others. It has six cycles, plus the four modifiers, so you do get plenty of options. Internally the baskets are average sized, the top one has a few tilted spaces for glass and cups etc, plus racks for plates, bowls so long as they aren't too big, none of the tines on the top rack are able to be moved so you're stuck with what Haier think a top rack should be. The bottom rack has two rows, the back row is adjustable and each set of tines can be lowered completely, but the front row which takes up half the width cannot be. The dishwasher cleaner dispenser is on the right side of the door and has a slide up, not a pop open, option, so you can I guess stack a tallish plate in there and it will still open and pop out your cleaner of choice. The left side is a blank space where the basket for cuttlery sits, its adequate, though lacks much space for utensils, and the little squares designed to hold cuttlery are small, so if you have knives or forks etc with wide handles you may also encounter a challenge wedging them in there. You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

You do have to jiggly the utensils and cuttlery about abit as you load the machine to prevent taller items and the middle spray arm having a wee accident.On the topic of spray arms there are three, one at the bottom pointing up, one in the middle which appears to direct water both up and down, and at the very top of the machine is another smallish arm that appears to direct more water down onto items in the top basket primarily. The additional third/upper spray arm is a nice to have, normal on higher end machines I think, so an unexpected item here.In terms of cleaning performance, I cannot fault it so far. For day to day dinner ware, cups, glasses and all the usual things this machine has performed very well. We use those blue and yellow tabs with the red spot, so not the posh ones, but also not just plain powder. I add rinse aid though in theory shouldn't need to, and the machine enables you to adjust the dose of rinse aid and the instructions are clearly shown in the user manual. I haven't yet had a single item come out not sparkly clean, I cannot fault the quality of the clean so far, and have mostly used either the medium or 60 min cycle, with the extra dry option. I haven't put anything too challenging in there, maybe the baskets from the airfryer are the worst, but i do hand wash these first, it will be interesting to see what its performance is like over the coming christmas rush, anything is possible.This Haier allows a number of other features from higher end machines, including the door that opens (quite a lot) at the almost end of the cycle, it seems to rely primarily on that to dry dishes, but you can turn this opening off so it would be interesting to see how well it dries if the door stays shut. It also has WIFI control by way of the SmartHQ app which I believe is the one Haier uses, it enables you to remotely turn on the machine, select the cycle and the add-ons and then start it, you can also use the timer via the app or on the machine to schedule the start time to take advantage of free or cheaper power.My only real criticism of this machine is that it is in my view too loud. Where we have it installed one side as well as the front are open/exposed, so it is not fully enclosed in an under bench space, we had to remove the top section which I guess isn't all that unusual, but there isn't a lot of padding in there to dampen sound, and you can certainly hear it when it is running, the configuration of dishes within seems to make no odds, nor does the load size generally, its just not a quiet machine in my situation. Maybe if it were built in on all sides the noise would be dampened more by cupboards as others do say it is very quiet. That is however my only critique of it, its cleaning performance has been excellent, the choice of cycles is good and more than meets our every day needs.Personally I have no hesitation in recommending a Haier product, both of the ones we now have, plus a dryer actually, have all been purchased in 2025, so it will be interesting to see if they make it to 2035.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher has been a disappointment from the moment it was installed and has only deteriorated from there.
Comments (English): [ QUALITY CONTROL WAS OPTIONAL ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher has been a disappointment from the moment it was installed and has only deteriorated from there. Build Quality. The overall construction is cheap and flimsy. Internal components feel lightweight, poorly supported, and clearly engineered to meet a price point rather than durability standards. This is not the build quality one expects from a major appliance brand. Cleaning Performance. Despite correct installation, proper loading, and quality detergent:. Dishes routinely come out still dirty. Utensils often retain visible debris. Plates and cookware frequently have greasy smears. Wash results are inconsistent and unreliable. This unit fails at the single job a dishwasher exists to perform. Serious Mechanical Defect (Within 60 Days). On 12/17/25, less than two months after installation, a plastic component was found loose inside the dishwasher tub. The part appears to be a thermoplastic pump bushing / sleeve from the circulation pump assembly. It shows clear heat deformation and partial melting on opposite sides, consistent with misalignment and friction from rotating components. This is not wear. This is not detergent damage. This is not user error. Plastic components do not melt symmetrically unless they were improperly installed or misaligned at the factory. The failure indicates poor assembly and inadequate quality control. Why This Is Unacceptable. A modern dishwasher should not:. Perform poorly from day one. Shed internal components into the wash cavity. Exhibit heat-damaged plastic parts within weeks of installation. This is a premature mechanical failure that strongly suggests broader reliability issues. Left uncorrected, defects like this typically lead to pump damage, sump cracking, leaks, and costly repairs once the warranty expires. Final Verdict. This dishwasher reflects cost-cutting design, weak materials, and poor manufacturing oversight. It has failed both functionally and mechanically in an unacceptably short time. I would strongly advise consumers to avoid this model. Based on this experience, I have serious concerns about GE's current dishwasher quality and long-term reliability. A dishwasher should clean dishes and stay intact. This one does neither.

Sentence (English): I was so excited for this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I wanted to love it so much ] || ---------------- || I was so excited for this dishwasher. After loads of research we decided to go with this machine. The layout is wonderful. I love how spacious it is as well as the LED lights within the tub itself. Unfortunately, that is where the positives end. The normal cycle consistently leaves me with dirty pans, glass bowls, and utensils. Non stick surfaces, glass and stainless steel— nothing is coming out clean. The cycle is quiet enough, and the contol panel is easy to use. But the only way I have a shot of getting clean dishes is using every cycle at max strength which takes a whopping five hours! I was so excited for the one hour cycle since we have three small kids and go through a lot of dishes, but frankly they would get cleaner sitting in a sink full of water than wasting the energy to load this machine. We had a Samsung machine that worked great but the control panel stopped working two weeks after the warranty ran out. I guess we will try to return this machine.

I wonder if it was the steamed egg that dried on it. It washes Chinese restaurant oil and all kinds of seasoning dirt really well. Comments (English): I placed the order and mistakenly put my work address as the delivery address. I called Home Depot the next day to verbally correct my mistake. Which was great, once I got the work I checked the order to ensure that the delivery address was updated. It wasn't. On the day of the delivery, I was nervous so I called Home Depot, they said everything was set up for delivery. Well once the delivery drives called me to give me a heads up that they would be coming in 15 minutes I verified that they had the correct address. They didn't. I am so glad that they driver called. I get that it was my initial mistake, but I reached out and spoke with more than 3 Home Depot employees, went on line to update and then called again to reconfirm. Home Depot dropped the ball in my opinion. The deliver driver confirmed that this happens all the time.

Sentence (English): The initial delivery/installers did not know to punch out the plug on the disposal unit before attaching the drain hose.
Comments (English): The initial delivery/installers did not know to punch out the plug on the disposal unit before attaching the drain hose. When we ran the dishwasher the first time we received an error code that indicated it didn't drain properly. Indeed , the bottom of the dishwasher was filled with water. When contacting customer service we opted to get a new replacement dishwasher. When that unit arrived I even mentioned to the installer that the plug still being there as a possibility. Despite that, when the installation was completed, we got the same error code. A third home visit was made and the service man immediately punched out that plug and the dishwasher has worked perfectly since then. Obviously, this was an inconvenience and makes me question the quality of the contracting company.f

We were not sure whether to get the version with protruding handle or the pocket handle, but decided on the pocket handle and like it. We run a load a night on average and it has done a good job cleaning/sterilizing our tableware. Two of the shelves are adjustable in height to accommodate different needs. The 3rd Party Company Best Buy used for install and haul away of the old dishwasher did a great job and reviewed the operation with a few tips. If it lasts a decade or more, we'll be happy with the purchase.

Sentence (English): I can't speak to the product because I never had the opportunity to use it.
Comments (English): [ Poor Communication & Customer Information ] || ---------------- || I can't speak to the product because I never had the opportunity to use it. I ordered a Bosch because it had the best reviews and I had an appliance technician tell me they were the best dishwashers. On the original delivery date I was given 24-hours in advance a four hour window for delivery. I had a commitment I could not move during 1 hour of the four- hour window. I called the number provided to adjust the time and was told there was no flexibility with the time and that I would have to schedule a different day. Fast forward a week later, same 24-hour notice. On the day of delivery I received a call an hour before the delivery window started that the installers would arrive in 15 min (luckily I work from home and could accommodate that). They arrived to tell me since I ordered a Bosch, it had its own “special” parts and I do not have the parts that are needed. NOWHERE on Costco's website for the Bosch dishwasher states there are specific parts needed for the install of this appliance. The installers said there was nothing they could do because I don't have the right part. So I had to return the dishwasher right then without any option or alternative. I now have to start all over. Costco service was very kind in taking my feedback and issuing the refund but now I have to start completely over. And since it's the holidays the earliest I can get a new dishwasher is after the new year - which is at least 2 more weeks. I will not order an appliance from Costco again.

Sentence (English): 1 star.
Comments (English): [ Broke in 7 Days — Warranty Nightmare ] || ---------------- || 1 star. The dishwasher failed within the first week of ownership. GE outsources warranty work to a third-party process (Bodewell), and getting help required repeated follow-ups. After filing the repair request, it took four calls to get meaningful progress. The service technician was professional and thorough, but he was a contractor and not actually employed by the warranty company.On the first visit, the technician identified a control panel that was faulty from the factory and ordered the required part. The repair was supposed to be completed before Thanksgiving, but the appointment was canceled, leaving us without a functioning dishwasher through the holiday (paper plates for Thanksgiving).After additional calls and escalation, Bodewell shipped a part directly to my house and scheduled the contractor to return—only for the shipment to be the wrong part. The technician then ordered the correct part and the repair is currently scheduled for 12/31/25. Despite that, on 12/17/25 I received an email stating the repair was “complete” and asking me to rate my experience. I emailed Bodewell for clarification and received no response. The technician deserves credit; the product quality and warranty administration do not.
